reason: The cited evidence shows that HEAs with BCC structure are superconducting (E1, E2) and mentions that disorder and electron count can impact superconductivity (E3), but none of the passages provide specific evidence that configurational entropy independently enhances electron-phonon coupling, minimizes scattering, or systematically raises Tc when electron count is held constant. The key mechanistic premises are therefore unsupported by the cited prior work.
premises: Configurational disorder (mixing entropy) can be tuned independently of average valence electron count
Higher configurational entropy enhances electron-phonon coupling and Cooper pairing
Higher configurational entropy minimizes detrimental electron scattering
A homogeneous but disordered BCC lattice stabilizes Cooper pairing
Tc and critical fields increase systematically with configurational entropy
